hero.eyebrow: Self-hosted · Free for personal and noncommercial use
hero.title: Run your whole table from one browser tab
hero.lead: TTRPG.Codex is a companion for running tabletop role-playing campaigns. One DM, any number of players: a live table with initiative, hit points and conditions; campaign prep and a world wiki; and a rules Library you can extend with homebrew. It ships with the Fifth Edition SRD 5.2.1, and other systems can be added as data.
hero.note: Windows, macOS and Linux · English, Русский, עברית
hero.shotAlt: The live table in TTRPG.Codex: initiative order with hit-point bars and conditions, the DM's controls and a dice tray.

features.title: Everything between sessions and at the table
features.lead: Built for the way a game actually runs: prepare quietly, then keep the table moving without a stack of tabs and paper.

items.title: A live table
items.text: Initiative, hit points, conditions with round counters, a dice tray and quick notes. Everyone sees changes the moment the DM makes them.

items.title: Character sheets from data
items.text: Sheets are drawn from the game system's own definition, with rule checks you can set to strict, warn or off, and level-up guidance from the Library.

items.title: Prep and a world wiki
items.text: Cast with portraits, a bestiary shortlist, regions and places, linked wiki pages with templates for what you write often, and lore you can reveal to one character or the whole party.

items.title: A Library you can extend
items.text: Ships with the Fifth Edition SRD 5.2.1. Write homebrew, clone an entry as a variant, and carry sets of it between campaigns as packs.

items.title: Sessions, recaps and journals
items.text: A player-facing recap and a separate DM summary, table notes (private or shared) and a private journal that not even the DM can read.

items.title: Secrets stay secret
items.text: NPCs can be hidden, met as strangers under a name you choose, or revealed. A shared page keeps its secrets, with what the players are told instead. Players only ever receive what they are allowed to see.

items.title: Optional AI, on your own key
items.text: Draft recaps, histories and characters, or build the world in a chat. Nothing is sent to a model until you click, and nothing is saved until you apply it.

items.title: Systems are data
items.text: A system is a YAML file plus packs of YAML content: attributes, resources, sheet fields, content types and conditions. Define your own without touching the program.

ai.title: Bring your own model, and stay in control
ai.text: Every “{{ui:Session.DraftAi}}” button talks to a chat model you choose. OpenRouter is pre-selected, with presets for OpenAI, Groq, Mistral, a local Ollama or LM Studio, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
bullets: Keys are stored encrypted on your server
Nothing goes to a model until someone clicks an AI button
The world builder proposes places, people, factions, quests and homebrew; you review each change and apply only what you want
Writes in the reader's language

how.title: From download to first session in minutes

steps.title: Install and start
steps.text: Run the installer. TTRPG.Codex sits in your system tray, starts the server and opens your browser.

steps.title: Create a campaign
steps.text: Make an account (the first becomes the server admin), create a campaign and pick a game system.

steps.title: Send the invite link
steps.text: Players open the link on their phone or laptop, create an account and join. Scan the QR code if you are in the same room.

systems.title: What is in the box, in plain terms
systems.lead: What ships today, what you can add, and what you may do with it.

panels.title: Ships with the Fifth Edition SRD 5.2.1
panels.text: Twelve classes, nine species, four backgrounds, seventeen feats, 339 spells and 340 creatures from the System Reference Document 5.2.1, used under CC BY 4.0. It is the one complete game system included today. TTRPG.Codex describes itself as "5E compatible" and has no connection to Wizards of the Coast.

panels.title: Built to take other systems
panels.text: A game system is data, not code: a YAML file for attributes, resources, sheet fields, content types and conditions, plus packs of entries. A small system, like the bundled d6 example, is one short file and a few entry files. Rules that need real logic, such as 5E's spell slots and level-ups, take a compiled plugin. Other publishers' content is not included.

panels.title: Free for personal and noncommercial use
panels.text: The program is source-available under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. Run it for your own table, your club or a class, and study and change it for noncommercial purposes. It is not an OSI open-source licence, and it does not allow selling it or using it commercially. Unsure whether your use counts? Open an issue and ask.

download.title: Get TTRPG.Codex
download.lead: Every package carries the .NET runtime it needs. Nothing else to install.
download.unsigned: The packages are not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper will ask before running them.
